threads.thread_goal: Align on candidate dishes and lock the final seasonal lunch menu list.

messages.text: Morning all. I have uploaded the first pass of the Seasonal Lunch Menu Draft as A1 for the Launch of a Seasonal Healthy Lunch Menu project. It covers 10 ideas split across meat, fish, vegetarian and vegan, based on what we can do with current kit and storage. This should also close out the first part of T1. Can you all have a look today and comment on what feels realistic for a 21‑day rollout, especially around prep time and any gaps on vegetarian or low‑allergen options?

Had a quick read through A1. Overall mix looks good, but I see only two fully vegan dishes and one vegetarian. For a healthy seasonal lunch, that might be a bit light. Also, the roasted veg grain bowl and the fish stew might clash on burner space at peak. We should check that against our current service window before we confirm the list for T1.

I like the look of the grilled chicken salad and the baked fish with herbs in A1. Both are straightforward with what we already do and fit the healthy angle. For the veg options, I think we can add another salad‑style dish quite easily, maybe something with beans and roasted veg, so it does not overload the hot line. That would still keep T1 manageable.

Agree with the comments so far. From a prep point of view, the soup of the day and the grain bowl in A1 can share a lot of vegetable prep if we plan it right. That helps with the 21‑day deadline. I am a bit worried about the stuffed peppers though, they can be fiddly and slow to portion consistently. Maybe we keep them only if we are sure they will not slow service.

I checked A1 as well. For allergens, the nut‑crusted fish and the yoghurt dressing on the chicken salad will need clear notes later, but for now I think they are fine to keep as candidates. I like the idea of another bean‑based salad like 9052 suggested, that should be simple to portion and plate fast.

Good call on the stuffed peppers. Given the 21‑day window and our current oven space, I suggest we drop stuffed peppers from the candidate list in A1 and instead add a cold bean and roasted veg salad as another vegetarian option. That keeps prep simpler and still fits the healthy brief. If no one objects, I will update A1 accordingly and mark that as the final candidate list for T1.

Dropping stuffed peppers and adding the bean and roasted veg salad works for me. That should also help with cost control later when we do the costing sheet, since beans and seasonal veg are cheaper than peppers with fillings. For the overall mix, how many vegetarian and vegan dishes do we want to lock in now so we can design recipes in T2 with that in mind?

From what I see in A1 after the change, we would have grilled chicken salad, baked fish, soup, grain bowl, nut‑crusted fish, and maybe one more meat dish, plus the two salads and one vegan hot dish. I would suggest at least three vegetarian or vegan dishes on the final menu so guests always see a strong plant‑based choice.

Three sounds reasonable, but given the healthy focus and the fact that we are not changing equipment, I think we can stretch to four vegetarian or vegan dishes without stressing the line. Two cold (salads or grain bowls) and two hot. That also gives front of house more to talk about. We just need to be sure the hot ones share prep where possible.

I can handle four veg or vegan dishes as long as we keep the steps clear on the recipe cards later. If we do two cold and two hot like you said, I can batch the veg prep in the morning and that should fit with our current opening hours.

Ok, proposal: we set the target at four vegetarian or vegan dishes on the final menu, with at least one fully vegan hot option. That gives us a clear rule for which candidates in A1 move forward into T2. If everyone is ok with that, we can mark that as our number and close that point.

Four veg or vegan dishes including one hot vegan works for me. For the meat and fish side, I would keep grilled chicken salad, baked fish with herbs, the soup of the day, and one lean meat special that we rotate weekly. That should give us a balanced list without overloading the grill or oven.

Let me summarise the candidate dishes we move forward from A1 into full recipe work for T2, based on this thread: 1) Grilled chicken salad with yoghurt dressing. 2) Baked herb fish. 3) Soup of the day (veg‑led, rotating). 4) Lean meat weekly special. 5) Grain bowl with roasted seasonal veg. 6) Bean and roasted veg salad. 7) Hot vegan stew or casserole. 8) Nut‑crusted fish, with clear allergen notes later. That gives us four vegetarian or vegan dishes and four meat or fish. If no one flags anything else, I will lock this list as the final seasonal lunch menu base.
List looks good to me and feels realistic for the 21‑day deadline. With that locked, I can start sketching prep steps for the grain bowl and the hot vegan stew so we are ready when we move into T2.
All good from my side as well. Once you update A1 with the final list, share the link again and we can use it as the single reference for recipe development and costing.

threads.thread_goal: Define recipes, portions, and costing for each approved dish.

messages.text: I have added first draft recipe cards for the eight agreed dishes into A2 and set up the initial costing in A3 for the Launch of a Seasonal Healthy Lunch Menu project. This covers a first pass on T2 and T3. Portions are currently set at what we usually plate, but I have not tuned them yet against the target food cost. Please review especially the grain bowl, hot vegan stew, and nut‑crusted fish, as they are closest to the cost limit.

I went through A3. Grain bowl and nut‑crusted fish are both a bit over the target food cost, mainly due to nuts and feta. The hot vegan stew is fine on cost but the portion might be larger than we need. In A2, the chicken salad and bean salad look straightforward. We should decide standard portion sizes now so we do not have to rework the cards later.

Looking at A2, the grilled chicken salad is set at 150 g chicken and a big handful of leaves. That might be generous for lunch. If we bring it down to around 120 g chicken and slightly more veg, we keep it filling but cheaper. Same idea for the grain bowl: a bit less grain, a bit more seasonal veg. That should help A3 numbers.

Agree on adjusting the balance rather than shrinking the plate. For the hot vegan stew in A2, we can keep the ladle size we use for our current soup and add a small side of grain or bread only on request. That keeps the base portion consistent and easier to cost in A3.

On the nut‑crusted fish in A2, could we reduce the nut mix slightly and add more herb crumb instead? That might keep the texture but lower the cost in A3. I am not fully sure how much we can cut without losing the crust, so I would like someone to double‑check the grams.

Yes, we can reduce the nut mix by about a third and bulk it with breadcrumbs and herbs. That should bring the food cost down without changing the look too much. I will update A2 and A3 with that change and re‑run the cost. For the chicken salad and grain bowl, I will also adjust the protein and veg balance as 9052 suggested.

Once those edits are in, we should lock standard portion sizes so everyone plates the same. Proposal: salads at 120 g cooked protein plus 150 g mixed veg and leaves, grain bowl at 180 g cooked grain plus 120 g veg, hot vegan stew at one full soup ladle, nut‑crusted fish at one fillet around 140 g. If we agree, we can mark that as our standard for T2 and T3.

Those portions sound good to me and match what we can plate quickly. With that, we just need to be strict on the scoop sizes and ladles. I will make sure the salad station has the right spoons ready once we move into prep planning.

Fine by me as well. For the soup of the day and the lean meat special in A2, can we just say they follow the same ladle and protein weights as the stew and chicken salad? That keeps things simple and should keep A3 within range too.

I have now updated A2 and A3 with the new portion sizes and the reduced nut mix. After recalculating, all dishes are within the target food cost range, with the nut‑crusted fish just under the limit. To stay safe on cost, I suggest we formally approve the nut‑to‑breadcrumb substitution and the protein reductions we discussed as our agreed changes.

Thanks for updating. With these portions and substitutions locked, I feel confident about prepping and plating consistently. I will start noting which utensils we need at each station so we do not drift from the agreed sizes during service.

Great. With D3 and the substitutions confirmed, T2 and T3 are in a good place. Next step from my side will be to double‑check supplier prices once more before launch, but that can run in parallel with prep planning.

threads.thread_goal: Set up prep workflow, food safety checklist, and allergen reference.

messages.text: Sharing a first pass at the daily prep schedule and batch plan for the new menu as part of T4, plus drafts of the Prep, Cleaning, and Food Safety Checklist in A4 and the Allergen and Dietary Reference Sheet in A6 for the Launch of a Seasonal Healthy Lunch Menu project. The schedule separates cold prep in the morning and hot prep closer to service. Please check if the timings and responsibilities look realistic, and also scan A6 for any missing allergens.

Looked at the T4 schedule. Overall flow makes sense, but the morning cold prep block might be tight if we get a big delivery. Maybe we move some veg washing to the previous afternoon when possible. On A4, I like that you called out cooling and reheating steps for the stew and soup. We should also add a quick check for fridge temps before we start batch cooking.

From the salad station side, the cold prep list in T4 is ok, but I would like a bit more buffer before service. If we can finish the bulk of salad veg 30 minutes earlier, I can set up the station calmly and double‑check labels. On A6, I noticed the yoghurt dressing is marked for dairy but not for any potential mustard in the dressing. We should confirm the recipe and update if needed.

I checked A6 for the hot vegan stew and grain bowl. Stew is correctly marked as vegan and gluten‑free, but the grain bowl might not always be gluten‑free depending on which grain we use. Maybe we should default to a gluten‑containing grain and clearly mark it, then offer a swap only if we have capacity. That way A6 stays accurate and we avoid confusion at the pass.

On A4, could we add a reminder about changing chopping boards between raw meat, fish, and veg during the morning prep block? I know it is standard, but having it on the checklist for the new menu will help me keep track when it gets busy.

Good catches. I will shift some veg washing to the previous afternoon in T4 and bring forward the salad prep by 30 minutes so you have that buffer. I will also add fridge temp checks at the start of hot prep in A4, and include a specific line about board changes and knife cleaning between raw and ready‑to‑eat items.

On the grain bowl in A6, I agree we should assume a standard grain that contains gluten and mark it clearly. If we ever offer a gluten‑free swap, we can treat that as a special and brief front of house separately. I will help double‑check all 14 major allergens across A6 once you have updated the dressing and grain notes.

I have now updated A6: yoghurt dressing flagged for dairy and mustard, grain bowl marked as containing gluten by default, and cross‑checked nuts and fish for the nut‑crusted fish. Please do a final scan so we can say the allergen sheet is ready for launch.

I checked A6 again. Chicken salad, bean salad, and grain bowl all look correctly tagged now. The only thing I added was a note that the soup of the day allergen info will be written on the board daily and must match the base recipe. From my side, the sheet is good to go.

Hot vegan stew and lean meat special entries in A6 look fine now. I also checked that the cooling and reheating steps in A4 line up with the allergen notes, so we do not mix up batches. No further changes from me.

The updated T4 schedule with some veg washing moved to the afternoon looks more realistic. I can handle the extra board changes and checks in A4 as long as we keep the checklist visible near the sink. That will help me tick things off as I go.

To wrap this up, can we confirm that the daily prep schedule in T4, with the adjusted timings and responsibilities, is our final plan for launch? If yes, we will print A4 and A6 and keep them at the pass and in the prep area as the single reference for safety and allergens.
Confirmed from my side. T4 schedule, A4 checklist, and A6 allergen sheet are ready to use. I will handle printing and posting them where needed before we start trial runs.

threads.thread_goal: Run tasting, refine recipes, and lock plating and service guidelines.

messages.text: Thanks for the tasting session earlier. I have logged the timing and feedback in A7 and drafted plating sketches and notes in A5 for all eight dishes, covering T7 and the first part of T5 and T8 for the Launch of a Seasonal Healthy Lunch Menu project. Overall timings were ok, but the grain bowl and hot vegan stew were a bit slow to plate. Please review A7 and A5 and share any final tweaks before we lock recipes and plating for launch.

Looking at A7, the main timing issue is the extra garnish steps on the grain bowl and the nut‑crusted fish. In A5, we can probably simplify by using one standard garnish for all salads and bowls, and one for hot mains. That should shave off a few seconds per plate without hurting presentation.

From the salad station, I felt the grilled chicken salad plating in A5 was a bit fussy with the separate drizzle and sprinkle steps. If we toss the leaves with dressing first and then place the sliced chicken on top, we can keep it neat and faster. The bean salad can follow the same pattern, which will help with consistency.

For the hot vegan stew, the tasting notes in A7 mention that the bowl looked a bit flat. In A5, maybe we can add a small spoon of chopped herbs on top and serve it in the slightly smaller bowl so it looks fuller. That should not add much time but will improve the look.

I struggled a bit with the nut‑crusted fish plating as drawn in A5. The angle of the fillet and the way the sauce was dotted around took me longer than the others. Could we switch to a simpler layout, like fish on top of the veg with sauce in one line, so it is easier to repeat?

All fair points. I will update A5 so that: salads and bean bowl use the same toss‑and‑top method, hot mains have one standard garnish, and the nut‑crusted fish sits on the veg with a single sauce line. For the stew, I will switch to the smaller bowl and add the herb sprinkle. Once I have edited A5, I will also adjust A2 where needed so the steps match.

After those edits, we should confirm that the recipe adjustments from A7 are fully reflected in A2 as well: slightly less grain in the bowls, the nut mix change, and the stew seasoning tweak we agreed during tasting. Once that is done, I am comfortable saying the recipes are final for launch.

I have now gone through A7 line by line and updated A2 accordingly: grain reduced and veg increased in the bowls, nut mix adjusted, stew seasoning and cooking time tweaked. With these changes in place, I suggest we mark the tasting feedback as fully applied and treat the recipes as final for this launch.

The updated salad plating in A5 looks much easier to execute. I can comfortably do that within the service window. I also like that the bean salad and chicken salad now look related but still distinct, which will help guests understand the menu quickly.

I checked the hot dishes in A5 after your edits. Stew in the smaller bowl with herbs on top looks better and did not slow me down in a quick test. Nut‑crusted fish on the veg with a single sauce line is also much simpler. From my side, the plating guide is ready to use.

I agree. With the simpler layouts in A5, I feel more confident about keeping up during busy periods. As long as we keep a printed copy near each station, I will be able to follow the standards without slowing down.

Given that A2 and A5 are now aligned with A7 and everyone is comfortable with the timing, I propose we formally approve these plating standards and service notes as final for launch. That way we can brief front of house and avoid last‑minute changes.
Agreed. I will export A5 as the final plating and service guide and share it with front of house along with a short briefing note. That should close out T5 and T8 for this phase.

threads.thread_goal: Plan launch week operations and agree on tracking of sales and waste.

messages.text: I have drafted the launch week service plan for the Launch of a Seasonal Healthy Lunch Menu project and added a simple Sales and Waste Log template in A8, covering T11 and T12. Plan assumes we launch in about two weeks, with slightly reduced regular menu during the first three days. Please review the proposed launch date, any temporary menu cuts, and the way A8 is set up for daily recording.

Looking at the T11 plan, the suggested launch date gives us a few days after the last trial to adjust if needed, which feels safe. I agree with trimming a couple of the heavier regular dishes for the first three days so the line is not overloaded. We just need to make sure front of house is briefed early.

I am fine with the launch date in the T11 draft. For the temporary menu reduction, I would suggest we pause the current pasta special and one of the fried items. That frees up space and attention for the new grain bowl and hot vegan stew, which are closer to the new menu style.

On A8, the columns for portions prepped, sold, and wasted are clear. Could we also add a quick note field for reasons of waste, like over‑prep or quality issue? That will help us adjust recipes or batch sizes after launch.

I had a look at A8 as well. I can fill it in at the end of my shift, but I would prefer if we agree who is responsible each day so it does not get forgotten. Maybe the person on closing prep can own it and quickly check numbers with the pass.
Good idea. I will add a short reason field to A8 and a line in T12 that the closing cook fills it in daily, checking with whoever is on the pass. That should keep the process simple and consistent.

I support pausing the pasta special and one fried item during launch week. That lines up with the healthy focus and frees up fryer and stove space. If everyone agrees, we can lock the proposed launch date from T11 and these temporary reductions as our plan.
Works for me. With those dishes paused, I can focus on the new salads and bowls without worrying about the pasta station. I will also keep an eye on portions so we do not over‑prep in the first days.

For recording in A8, I suggest we do a quick two‑step routine: note down portions prepped at the start of service, then at close write sold and waste with reasons. That should take only a couple of minutes if we keep the sheet open on the tablet.

I can handle that routine when I am on closing. If we rotate closing duties, we just need to remind whoever is closing that day to update A8. Maybe we add a small note about it to the end‑of‑day cleaning checklist so it is not missed.

Good call. I will add a reminder about updating A8 to the end‑of‑day section of A4 so it becomes part of the closing routine. With that, I think we can agree that the closing cook, with a quick check from the pass, will record sales and waste every day during launch week.

Perfect. I will update T11 with the confirmed launch date and the list of temporarily paused dishes, and we will brief front of house on the plan and on how we are using A8. That should set us up well for launch week.
